title.rendered: Pentecost Sunday: The Fire Has Fallen — The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Today is Pentecost Sunday. The fire that fell on the upper room is the fire that still burns in every believer. The wind that filled the house is your breath.

content.rendered:
Today is Pentecost Sunday. The fire that fell on the upper room two thousand years ago is the fire that still burns in every believer in Christ. The wind that filled the house is the breath you draw this morning. This is the day our reality was forged.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, May 24, 2026 · Pentecost Sunday

Today’s Scripture

“When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting. They saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.”
Acts 2:1–4 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Today is the day. Two thousand years ago, in a small upper room in Jerusalem, the Holy Spirit was poured out on a hundred and twenty people, and the church was born. Every gathering of believers around the world this morning is gathered because that day happened. From Lagos to London, from Nairobi to New York, from a megachurch to a living room in a village no one has heard of—the global church traces its breath back to the wind that filled that house.

Read Luke’s account again and feel the weight of it. A sound like a violent wind, blowing from heaven. Tongues of fire, dividing and resting on each one of them. Every disciple filled with the Holy Spirit. Every disciple speaking in other languages as the Spirit enabled them. Before the day was over, three thousand people were saved. The Spirit did not arrive politely. He arrived in fullness. He arrived loud. He arrived to stay.

But notice something often missed in the noise of the wind and the brightness of the fire. The wind and the fire were external signs. The real miracle of Pentecost was internal. They were filled with the Spirit. The Spirit went in. The same Spirit who hovered over the waters at creation, who anointed the prophets and the kings of Israel, who descended on Jesus at His baptism—that Spirit came to dwell inside ordinary men and women. That was the miracle of Pentecost. The temple was no longer a building. The temple was a person.

Two thousand years later, every believer in Jesus Christ is filled with the same Spirit who fell that morning. Not a different Spirit. Not a smaller portion. Not a lesser gift. The same Holy Spirit who set the upper room on fire is the Holy Spirit who lives in you right now. The fire that fell that day is not a museum artifact. It still burns.

If you ask the New Testament what the church is, this is the answer. The church is the people the Spirit was poured out on. We are not a religious institution. We are the dwelling place of God on the earth. Every person in Christ is a temple. Every gathering of believers is the manifest body. Every act of love and mercy and witness in this week is the fire that fell at Pentecost still burning in the world.

Today, lean in. Worship today with awareness of where you have come from. The wind that filled the house of those one hundred and twenty still moves. The fire that lit on their heads still burns. The Spirit who filled their lungs still fills yours every breath of this day. Pentecost is not a memory. Pentecost is your address.

Prayer

Father, thank You for the day You poured out Your Spirit. Thank You that the fire that fell on the upper room did not die with the disciples but continues to burn in every believer through every generation to this very morning. Today, on Pentecost Sunday, fill me afresh with the awareness of Your presence in me. Let me worship as one who knows where I have come from and Whose I am. Let the church around the world be set on fire again. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Today is Pentecost. The same Spirit who fell on the upper room lives in me. The fire has not gone out. The wind has not died down. The promise has not been recalled. I am filled. I am sealed. I am sent. The day God filled has come again, and He fills me afresh in it. I am the temple of the living God.
